chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from Jarrah al-Mad'ini from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The purchase of stolen goods and deceit is not valid if they are known."
ai.seo_question: What is the validity of buying stolen goods in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that the sale of stolen goods or items acquired through deceit is invalid (*salih*) provided the defect is known to the buyer. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that commercial validity requires the absence of hidden defects (*gharar*) and clear ownership, ensuring fairness in market transactions. It highlights the importance of transparency and the prohibition of trading in illicitly acquired property within Islamic economic ethics.
